blocks.body: Present Perfect: Negatives — haven't / hasn't + V3 for actions that have not happened or finished yet and experiences someone has never had.

{"level":"A2–B1","intro":"In negative Present Perfect sentences, we use have not / has not + V3 or the short forms haven't / hasn't.","rules":[{"label":"haven't / hasn't + V3","color":"emerald","text":"The negative is built with have / has, not with do / does.","example":"I haven't finished. / She hasn't called."},{"label":"Yet / not yet","color":"blue","text":"Yet normally goes at the end when an expected action is still incomplete. More formally, not yet can go before V3.","example":"We haven't eaten yet. / We haven't yet eaten."},{"label":"Never — without not","color":"amber","text":"Never already has a negative meaning, so do not add not.","example":"He has never seen snow. (Not: He hasn't never seen snow.)"}]}

{"title":"1. Basic negative patterns","intro":"Start with have / has, then add not and V3. Never replaces not; it is not used together with it.","items":[{"label":"I / You / We / They","title":"haven't + V3","subtitle":"I haven't finished. / They haven't arrived."},{"label":"He / She / It","title":"hasn't + V3","subtitle":"She hasn't called. / It hasn't started."},{"label":"Yet / not yet","title":"haven't + V3 + ... yet","subtitle":"We haven't done it yet. Also correct but more formal: We haven't yet done it."},{"label":"Full forms","title":"have not / has not","subtitle":"Both forms are correct, but haven't / hasn't usually sound more natural in speech."}]}

{"title":"2. When we use the negative","sections":[{"label":"No result yet","color":"emerald","description":"An expected action has still not produced a result up to now.","examples":[{"en":"I haven't found my keys yet.","ua":"The result is still missing."},{"en":"She hasn't finished her report.","ua":"The task is still not complete."}]},{"label":"No experience","color":"blue","description":"Never means that someone has not had the experience at any time up to now; it does not take not.","examples":[{"en":"We have never tried this dish.","ua":"No such experience up to now."},{"en":"He has never flown alone.","ua":"He has had no such experience."}]},{"label":"Period up to now","color":"amber","description":"A negative can describe no event in a period that is still open, or a state that has continued for only a short time.","examples":[{"en":"I haven't seen her this week.","ua":"This week is not finished yet."},{"en":"They haven't lived here for long.","ua":"They have lived here, but only for a short time."}]}]}

{"title":"3. Quick patterns","intro":"Compare not yet, never, and a finished past period.","rows":[{"en":"I haven't finished the task yet.","ua":"haven't + finished + yet","note":"an expected action is still incomplete"},{"en":"She hasn't called us today. / She didn't call us yesterday.","ua":"today is still in progress / yesterday is a finished period","note":"Present Perfect / Past Simple"},{"en":"We have never been to Berlin.","ua":"have never been — without not","note":"experience up to now"},{"en":"He hasn't found a job yet.","ua":"hasn't + found + yet","note":"the result is still missing"}],"warning":"Build the negative as haven't / hasn't + V3. Do not add not to never; use Past Simple with a finished-time expression such as yesterday."}

{"title":"4. Common mistakes","items":[{"label":"Mistake 1","color":"rose","title":"Replacing Present Perfect with do / does + V1.","wrong":"❌ I don't finish my work yet.","right":"✅ I haven't finished my work yet."},{"label":"Mistake 2","color":"amber","title":"Using V2 instead of V3.","wrong":"❌ She hasn't went home.","right":"✅ She hasn't gone home."},{"label":"Mistake 3","color":"sky","title":"Putting yet between V3 and its object.","wrong":"❌ We haven't finished yet the task.","right":"✅ We haven't finished the task yet. / We haven't yet finished the task."},{"label":"Mistake 4","color":"violet","title":"Adding not to never.","wrong":"❌ He hasn't never seen snow.","right":"✅ He has never seen snow."}]}

{"title":"5. Short summary","items":["The negative in the Present Perfect = haven't / hasn't + V3.","Use haven't with I / you / we / they and hasn't with he / she / it.","Not yet means an expected action has not happened or been completed; never means there has been no such experience at any time.","Never is already negative: use have never, not haven't never.","Yet normally goes at the end; the more formal haven't yet + V3 is also correct.","Use Past Simple with a finished-time expression such as yesterday. Exercises with yet follow British English."]}

{"title":"6. Practice","select_title":"Exercise 1. Choose the correct form","select_intro":"Choose the correct negative sentence in the Present Perfect.","selects":[{"label":"a) She hasn't finished the report yet. / b) She haven't finished the report yet.","prompt":"Which option is correct?","answer":"a"},{"label":"a) He hasn't never seen snow. / b) He has never seen snow.","prompt":"Which option is correct?","answer":"b"}],"options":["a","b"],"input_title":"Exercise 2. Build the sentence","input_intro":"Put the words in the correct order.","inputs":[{"before":"yet / hasn't / he / found / his keys","after":"→","accepted":["He hasn't found his keys yet.","He hasn't yet found his keys."]},{"before":"never / has / she / flown / alone","after":"→","answer":"She has never flown alone."}]}
